title: The formal inertia extension is controlled by a class, but the quotient and action need to be retained
place: Author p.5: exact sequence and self-intersection classification sentence.
body: At scan 096, “[self-intersection de X₀ dans 𝓧]” accompanies the claim that the tame fundamental-group extension is determined by the base and a degree-two class, with a preceding map from Π₂ᵗ to μᵗ∞. This supports Hua, findings register, `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection`, and Hua’s modernised reading, “L’énoncé” (p.95), while “Lemme 2 : la classe est celle de l’auto-intersection” (p.89, outside the supplied scans) adds the proposed construction of the inertia quotient. A careful formulation must retain that quotient and its base-group action; this leaf does not prove a general central or split extension theorem.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Le théorème, et deux exemples (pages 95 et 97)” → “L’énoncé” (Hua p.95 = scan 096; lines 2438–2461); antecedents “Le π₁ modéré d’un schéma formel le long de sa fibre spéciale (pages 87 et 89)” → “La suite exacte”, “Lemme 1 : le revêtement universel modéré n’a pas de H¹”, and “Lemme 2 : la classe est celle de l’auto-intersection” (Hua pp.87,89 = scans 088,090, outside supplied evidence; lines 2277–2383). Antecedent scans 088 and 090 are outside this package.
relation: frozen page supports/restates the extension–self-intersection connection in external finding `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection`; earlier context adds a proposed Hochschild–Serre/Hurewicz mechanism and an explicit warning about passing from μ to its inertia quotient. It does not license calling the complete proof present on scan 096.

title: Arithmetic centrality is an overstatement in the context
place: Scan 096 extension sequence; scan 098 arithmetic examples; cancelled scan 104 relation (6.4). The refuted adjective occurs in context, not scan 096.
body: The arithmetic examples of scan 098 and `fgf^{-1}=g^q` on cancelled scan 104 require caution with the adjective “central” in Hua, findings register, `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection`, and Hua’s “La suite exacte” (p.87). For the formal disc over F₂, the tame extension F₄((u))/F₂((t)), `u³=t`, has inertia C₃ conjugated by Frobenius through inversion, so that inertia is not central. This refutes that unrestricted contextual formulation; the extension must retain its cyclotomic action, or centrality must be restricted to circumstances in which the action on the relevant inertia quotient is trivial.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29: “La suite exacte”, Hua p.87 = scan 088 (outside package), lines 2306–2311: “L’extension est centrale”; repeated in `RESULTS_STATE` finding `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection`. Compare “La relation, et d’où elle vient”, Hua p.103 = scan 104, lines 2679–2694; “L’énoncé le plus précis”, Hua pp.121–122 = scans 122–123, lines 3148–3167, expressly requires triviality of the Tate sheaf to remove path dependence. Hua pp.121–122 → archive scans 122–123 are also outside this package; only contextual reading of that continuation was used.
relation: our direct algebraic example contradicts the context’s unrestricted adjective “central”, not the wording of scan 096. The later context adds/supports the needed attention to cyclotomic twisting. A chosen basis of a Tate module does not make a nontrivial Galois action trivial.
reason: An explicit tame degree-six extension over F₂((t)) has inertia C₃ with nontrivial Frobenius conjugation; this directly refutes unrestricted arithmetic centrality in the context, while leaving the source wording intact.

title: “Extension triviale” does not follow from Π₂=0
place: Example I, first case, ending with the underlined phrase “extension triviale”.
body: Scan 096 calls the extension “triviale” when the punctured curve is not P¹, and Hua’s “Exemple I” (p.95) repeats this as a separation of fibre and monodromy. If “triviale” means split, the stated vanishing of Π₂ is insufficient: a base with Π₂=0 can carry a nonzero central-extension class, as the Heisenberg extension of Z² shows. The useful next check is the Chern class of the normal bundle—especially its degree for a proper positive-genus curve—rather than an inference from Π₂ alone; the current package does not establish a general splitting.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29: “Exemple I : une courbe sur un corps algébriquement clos”, Hua p.95 = scan 096, lines 2463–2477. Context repeats “triviale” and adds “La monodromie et le groupe fondamental de la fibre se séparent, et il n’y a rien à calculer.” Compare “Lemme 2 : la classe est celle de l’auto-intersection”, pp.89/scan 090, and “Le programme kummérien : la classe, une deuxième fois”, p.100/scan 101. Hua p.89 → archive scan 090 is outside this package. The final unprimed D₀ on scan 096 is preserved as a reading issue, not normalised.
relation: Hua restates the literal claim and adds an unwarrantedly confident splitting gloss. The logical diagnostic differs from that gloss: vanishing Π₂ eliminates a left-hand obstruction but does not itself kill the degree-two extension class. It is not a geometric counterexample to every possible hidden hypothesis from the preceding leaves.
reason: The Heisenberg extension gives a complete counterexample to the bare inference Π₂=0 implies splitting; no geometric counterexample to all implicit hypotheses of the formal-curve claim is asserted.

title: The P¹ computation needs a degree-zero convention
place: Scan 096 multiplication-by-degree discussion; scan 098 Example I.2, the P¹/no-boundary case.
body: In the P¹ case scan 098 identifies the group with μₙ, where n is the prime-to-p part of the self-intersection degree, as repeated by Hua’s “Exemple I” (pp.95,97). Conditional on scan 096’s exact sequence and multiplication-by-degree map, degree zero gives the full tame Tate group as cokernel, while nonzero degree gives a finite cyclic quotient of order the prime-to-p part of its absolute value. The formula therefore needs either a degree-zero convention or an explicit nonzero-degree hypothesis; the leaf supplies neither.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29: “Exemple I : une courbe sur un corps algébriquement clos”, Hua pp.95,97 = scans 096,098, lines 2478–2491. Hua repeats μₙ and then illustrates negative self-intersection `−d`, without specifying degree zero.
relation: restates the nonzero-degree formula; our observation adds the zero-degree boundary and explicitly conditions the calculation on the displayed exact sequence and the asserted multiplication map. Related state ID: `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection`.
reason: The cokernel computation on the product of prime-to-characteristic Tate modules is elementary and explicit, conditional on the manuscript’s exact sequence and degree map; the geometric hypotheses themselves are not independently proved.

title: The arithmetic Π₂ question remains an explicit question
place: Example II.b, final question followed by three question marks.
body: Scan 098 ends its calculation of the allowed tame roots of unity on `Spec Z−S` with “Mais qu’est Π₂ᵗ(X₀/D′₀) ???”. Hua’s “Exemple II : les entiers” (p.97) restates this open question, and his later “Le calcul” under “π₂ contre la tour des revêtements” (pp.175–176, outside the supplied scans) adds a possible approach through cohomology of covering towers. Neither context nor the cited results register supplies this arithmetic Π₂ calculation.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29: “Exemple II : les entiers”, Hua p.97 = scan 098, lines 2493–2531; “π₂”, Hua p.104 = scan 105, lines 2731–2753; “π₂ contre la tour des revêtements (pages 175 et 176)” → “Le calcul”, pp.175–176 = scans 176–177, outside supplied images, lines 4388–4436. The covering-tower continuation at archive scans 176–177 is outside this package.
relation: Hua restates the question without answering it; later context adds a covering-tower/Hochschild–Serre route, not a calculation for the arithmetic base in scan 098. The present `RESULTS_STATE` has no matching solved entry.

title: Arithmetic finiteness/nonabelianity must remain a reading question
place: Example II.a, uncertain negative clause after the abelianization formula and concluding question marks.
body: On scan 098 the “sans doute” passage and its uncertain negative wording concern the whole tame group after the abelianization has been displayed, and end with question marks about nonabelian tame number fields. Hua’s “Exemple II” (p.97) instead paraphrases a finite-group claim “par dévissage”; this differs from the frozen reading and supplies no proof on the supplied leaf. Preserve the arithmetic assertion as unresolved in wording and scope rather than treating the computed abelianization as a finiteness proof for the full group.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29: “Exemple II : les entiers”, Hua p.97 = scan 098, lines 2510–2519, says “le groupe entier doit être fini par dévissage”.
relation: context differs from the frozen uncertain wording. It cannot be upgraded to a definite contradiction in the author's intended assertion without the reading being resolved, and it cannot be used to repair the frozen transcription. No relevant settled result in `RESULTS_STATE`.

title: Semi-global Abhyankar: local commutation proof stops
place: Surviving semiglobal Abhyankar paragraph, proof of b) and unfinished proof of c).
source_words: Étude locale en un pt de
body: Scan 100 reduces the proposed semiglobal Abhyankar statement to residual-characteristic control and “Commutation des Iᵢ”, but the final local argument stops at “en un pt de”. Hua’s “Une version semi-globale du résultat d’Abhyankar” (p.99) restates the result and calls the local computation classical, which is an addition to this leaf rather than a written completion. Any reconstruction should use the revised henselian-pair hypothesis and primes invertible along the relevant divisor, and should distinguish pairwise commutation of the inertia factors from centrality under the full fundamental group.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29: “Abhyankar semi-global, et la même classe une deuxième fois (pages 99 et 100)” → “Une version semi-globale du résultat d’Abhyankar”, Hua p.99 = scan 100, lines 2533–2572.
relation: Hua restates the three conclusions but adds that the calculation is classical and identifies it with logarithmic inertia; those comments do not complete the proof on scan 100. The frozen page adds/retains the revised henselian-pair hypothesis, globally invertible primes, and the visible change “produit” → “groupe engendré”, details smoothed in context. Related to the mechanism of `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection`, but not a proof of its global classification.

title: Kummer–Chern equality is explicitly a programme
place: Circled 1, extension class and displayed Chern-class target near the foot of the page.
body: “On veut prouver” on scan 101 identifies the pulled-back group-extension class with the tuple of Kummer Chern classes `c(Oₓ(Dᵢ)) mod nᵢ`. Hua’s “Le programme kummérien” (p.100) restates this and adds a connection to the formal self-intersection lemma (p.89) and to the later divisor gerbe (p.200, both outside the supplied evidence), linking the leaf to Hua, findings register, `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection`. The useful research step is a cocycle comparison with the specified twisted coefficient sheaf; this page announces, but does not carry out, that comparison.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29: “Le programme kummérien : la classe, une deuxième fois”, Hua p.100 = scan 101, lines 2574–2623; earlier “Lemme 2 : la classe est celle de l’auto-intersection”, p.89 = scan 090; later “Les exemples kummériens, et la classe une quatrième fois (pages 199 et 200)” → “Exemple 2 : des diviseurs, et la gerbe”, Hua p.200 = scan 201, outside package, lines 5177–5215. Hua p.89 → archive scan 090 and p.200 → archive scan 201 are outside this package.
relation: Hua restates the target and adds the link to the four occurrences of the same obstruction class, including the later gerbe interpretation. This supports `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection` at the level of a shared programme, not as a completed proof on scan 101.

title: Extension to formal schemes or ringed topoi is not developed here
source_words: Variantes schémas formels (ou topos loc. annelés généraux)
body: Scan 101’s “Variantes schémas formels (ou topos loc. annelés généraux)” proposes carrying the Kummer–Chern identification beyond schemes. Hua’s “Le programme kummérien” (p.100) repeats the direction and connects it to the formal calculation and later gerbe language, but supplies no theorem for arbitrary locally ringed topoi. A formulation would have to specify the topology, the exactness of the chosen Kummer sequence, and the descent data for the root objects before importing the cohomological identity.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29: “Le programme kummérien : la classe, une deuxième fois”, Hua p.100 = scan 101, lines 2620–2623; earlier formal version pp.87–97, and later divisor-gerbe pp.199–200. Earlier formal discussion Hua pp.87–93 → archive scans 088–094 is outside this package; Hua pp.95,97 → scans 096,098 are supplied. Later divisor-gerbe discussion Hua pp.199–200 → scans 200–201 is outside this package.
relation: Hua restates the closing direction and adds the earlier/later parallels, without supplying a general ringed-topos theorem. `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection` concerns the formal-scheme specialisation only.

title: The corollary’s inertia coefficient identification needs its own hypotheses
place: Circled 3, Corollaire: deleted commutation/product clauses, surviving twisted inertia coefficient, and normal-bundle conclusion.
body: Scan 103’s “Corollaire” deletes the separate pairwise-commutation clause and a product description of inertia before asserting the class of the normal bundle. Hua’s “Le théorème kummérien, troisième énoncé” (p.102) restates the intended Kummer identification, but the cancelled text should not be silently restored: invariant cyclic subgroups alone need not commute, as the two order-four subgroups of Q₈ show. The remaining task is to identify the geometric hypothesis or argument that makes the surviving inertia coefficient abelian and identifies its twist with the displayed roots-of-unity sheaf; the page does not write it out.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29: “Le théorème kummérien, troisième énoncé”, Hua p.102 = scan 103, lines 2646–2675. Hua says the frozen material is hard to read, states an extension with coefficient I and a product-of-μ identification, and records the targeted normal-bundle class.
relation: Hua restates the overall conclusion but smooths/differs from the cancellations and remaining uncertainty about the inertia coefficient. The context's normal-bundle interpretation agrees with the last line; it does not justify restoring a cancelled product decomposition. Related ID: `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection`.

title: Cancelled quasi-unipotence lemma: the elementary ending is valid, but context changes the stated reading
place: Entire cancelled face, Lemma6.5 and unfinished eigenvalue argument.
body: On scan 104, “deux automorphismes” and `FGF⁻¹=G^q` lead to quasi-unipotence, but the cancelled proof stops after choosing repeated powers of an eigenvalue. An independent check completes the argument: the finite nonzero spectrum is permuted by q-th powering, so every eigenvalue is a root of unity and a common power of G is unipotent. Hua’s “Le lemme” (p.103) supplies this ending but says the source had “endomorphismes”, a reading discrepancy with the frozen text; its account of why the page was cancelled is not established by these scans. This does not add to LM1 E.2 or close LM1 E.11, which concern group schemes over rings rather than this finite-dimensional field calculation.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29: “Le théorème de monodromie locale (pages 103 et 104)” → “Le lemme”, Hua p.103 = scan 104, lines 2696–2729; editorial header lines 38–44. Hua’s footnote says the source reads “deux endomorphismes” and supplies invertibility, contrary to the frozen reading. Hua adds an SGA7 attribution and interpretation of the cancellation; neither is independently checked here.
relation: context restates the mathematical automorphism lemma and adds its ending; differs on the underlying word and on its explanation of cancellation. LM1 E.2 remains background only: no new exp/log theorem is obtained. LM1 E.11 remains open in the register.

title: H² defines a pro-Pi₂ only after the coefficient and universal-cover conventions are fixed
place: Top half, a) left-exact H² coefficient functor and b) universal-pointed-cover definition.
body: Scan 105 defines Π₂ from `M↦H²(X,M)` and explicitly says “exact à g.” for a simply connected X before passing to the universal pointed cover in general. For finite abelian constant coefficients, the long exact cohomology sequence explains that left exactness once H¹ vanishes, but the leaf does not specify the site, the treatment of the pro-cover, or the comparison with a higher homotopy construction. Hua’s “π₂” (p.104) restates the definition and calls it étale homotopy, while “Le calcul” on pp.175–176 (outside this package) adds a covering-tower framework; these are useful comparisons, not a proof of those omitted identifications on scan 105.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29: “π₂” under “Le théorème de monodromie locale”, Hua p.104 = scan 105, lines 2731–2753; “Lemme 1 : le revêtement universel modéré n’a pas de H¹”, Hua p.89 = scan 090, lines 2313–2343; “π₂ contre la tour des revêtements (pages 175 et 176)” → “Le calcul”, Hua pp.175–176 = scans 176–177, lines 4393–4436; compare “Quand un foncteur est pro-représentable”, Hua pp.181–185 = scans 182–186, lines 4576–4611, concerning a different set-valued functor/strictness setup. Hua p.89 → scan 090, pp.175–176 → scans 176–177, and pp.181–185 → scans 182–186 are outside this package.
relation: Hua restates pro-representability and adds an identification with étale homotopy and later covering-tower context, but writes “exact” where the frozen source says “exact à g.”. The latter distinction should be retained. No RESULTS_STATE row settles this exact construction; finite-model results elsewhere in the register address another problem.

title: Functorial inertia begins with dependence on a prolongation
place: Inertia definition by a stabilizer; warning about dependence on prolongation and the normalisation convention.
body: Scan 117 insists that the inertia conjugacy class “dépend du choix du prolongement”, with normalisation chosen under the stated normality hypothesis. Hua’s “1. Ce qu’est un groupe d’inertie, et de quoi il dépend” (p.116) restates this, and “2. Fonctorialité” adds the inclusion of stabilizers once an equivariant prolongation exists. Thus the research issue is to track that prolongation and its existence through a morphism, not to treat a boundary point alone as determining canonical inertia; scan 117 itself does not yet prove the later functorial claims.

Ce qu’est un groupe d’inertie, et de quoi il dépend”, Hua p.116 = scan 117, lines 2962–2990; “2. relation: context restates the dependence and normalisation convention, then adds the equivariant-prolongation inclusion and local branch calculation from continuation pages not proved on scan 117. Related ID `29-inertia-matrix-determinant` is downstream, not a claim appearing on this supplied leaf.

title: The determinant finding is a context-only continuation, not a verified manuscript result here
place: Context-only continuation of the supplied inertia setup; archive scan 121, the determinant-finding witness, is absent from this package.
body: Hua, findings register, `29-inertia-matrix-determinant`, concerns Hua p.120, hence archive scan 121, which is absent from this package; scan 117 supplies only the opening inertia definitions. Hua’s “4. La matrice des multiplicités” says that pullback multiplicities give N and that, for equal branch counts, invertibility is equivalent to `det N=±pʳ` (p the characteristic exponent, p=1 in characteristic zero), but attributes only the matrix-algebra equivalence to its Lean check. The geometric identification of the inertia map, the conjugacy consequence, and the source’s exact hypotheses remain unverified here, and the lack of a reference in that project is not evidence of novelty.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29: “4. La matrice des multiplicités” under “Comportement fonctoriel…”, Hua p.120 = archive scan 121, lines 3043–3108. The footnote reports a Lean check of the algebraic determinant equivalence and expressly excludes the geometric identification with N and conjugacy conclusion; no Lean file is supplied or run here. “L’énoncé le plus précis”, Hua pp.121–122 = scans 122–123, adds path/Tate-sheaf qualification and reports marginal “Remords au nᵒ3,4” (context only in this support assignment). Archive scans 121–123 are outside this package; no image or formalization file for the external finding was inspected.
relation: context adds the matrix statement to the supplied page 117 setup; the package cannot confirm its original wording, hypotheses, corrections or proof on scan 121. `RESULTS_STATE` credits this to Hua, findings register, `29-inertia-matrix-determinant` and says “new to us”; it is not an established novelty result. The modernised file calls it probably known and says the cited literature search did not find the explicit determinant/conjugacy formulation.

title: The cancelled pro-ℓ image fragment is not part of the surviving Abhyankar proof
place: Cancelled opening fragment and inertia square, before the horizontal separator.
source_words: qui opère sur $E$ via un pro-$\ell$-groupe
body: Before the surviving Abhyankar paragraph, scan 100 cancels the claim that a finite-index subgroup acts on E through a pro-ℓ group, followed by “À fortiori” and an inertia square. Hua’s “Une version semi-globale du résultat d’Abhyankar” (p.99) omits this fragment; his later “Le lemme” (p.103) concerns quasi-unipotence but supplies no missing topology or coefficient hypotheses for it. This is a possible representation-theoretic link to the monodromy draft, with no completed inference or reason for cancellation preserved here.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29: “Une version semi-globale du résultat d’Abhyankar”, Hua p.99 = scan 100, lines 2538–2572, starts with the surviving semiglobal argument and does not reproduce this fragment; related “Le lemme” at Hua p.103 = scan 104 treats a linear quasi-unipotence conclusion, not the topological pro-ℓ-image assertion. Global searches for `pro-`, `indice fini`, `opère sur … E`, and `ell`-adic terms found no explicit treatment of this cancelled statement in the modernised file.
relation: the frozen source adds a cancelled representation-theoretic lead omitted by Hua's account. No `RESULTS_STATE` entry settles the fragment with its unspecified representation hypotheses; LM1 E.2 is not an answer.
